As an EM/dbus-sensors maintainer, I'm not interested in supporting two different ways of representing DBus.  Supporting the one we have is difficult enough and what's proposed here isn't any simpler.  Unfortunately what we have today does allow PDI-based reactors to function, so I'm going to spend time, it likely won't be on this.

If there are other reactor maintainers that want to band together and work through all the use cases to make this work, I'm in full support of staging that effort under an option key once we get enough critical mass.

I do worry that we've left out a ton of requirements, and every one of these requirements is based on DBus.  We need to refocus them on the developer and the user part of the requirements.  I would far prefer very messy internal DBus structures, and functional user/developer APIs to the alternative.  If we can have both, I'm in full support, and will likely help, but I don't think this as written gets us there, and the requirements need to be updated to reflect the users of this software, not the developers of this software.

IMO EM and reactors don't follow these guidelines because they do not allow for ad-hoc changes. Not because of some real technical limitation. It's more of a workflow issue.

The guidelines present patterns for

- adding properties 
- removing properties
- changing property type
- representing optional data

and various other issues. The guidelines apply far beyond just OpenBMC.

If you have some alternative workflow for designing and changing DBus interfaces i would encourage you to document it somewhere alongside it's technical merits and how it is a better workflow for OpenBMC specifically.

If it's undocumented ad hoc workflow then i don't get how that works in presence of a well documented guideline and existing tooling.

> How do you draw this conclusion?

Because I was present when EM was created, before it was called EM and was a python script 😄 and had discussed the design intent with the author at length.

> Can you link to any DBus or systemd related source where people are using unbounded sets of DBus interfaces?

> because they do not allow for ad-hoc changes.

> If you have some alternative workflow for designing and changing DBus interfaces
Option 1.
1. Keep dbus interfaces non typesafe.
2. Write code that on clients that can parse both the old and the new interfaces.
3. Write code on the producer that produces the new interface
4. (optional, and probably not prefered) remove the code from the clients that parses the old way.

You can look at converting Sensor values from int -> double as an example of this.  Not sure how we could've accomplished that in a PDI client.

Option 2: Do what systemd and other dbus interfaces do, and apply a version number to your interfaces, rolling it when there's incompatible changes made.

>  EM's representation for arrays goes completely against the grain.

1000000% agreed.  The problem is do we break things that are working to make it the internal APIs better?  There's really not that many arrays in EM, and most of the objects are flat (the new firmware update stuff messes that up a bit).

> Sure, systemd itself adds new interfaces as required, and doesn't use PDI.

This isn't an example of an "unbounded sets of DBus interfaces".  You are correct that they don't document using PDI but, you **can** actually document them with PDI and have PDI-based clients interact with systemd.  We have `com.freedesktop.UPower.Device` already documented exactly this way.

To me there are 3 things that EM especially does that do not conform to either the spec explicitly or generally accepted practices:

* Interfaces having properties missing in some instances.
* Interface instances having differing types for the same property in different instances.
* Unique interfaces with numbers prepended as an "instance value" rather than a different path. [ie. the array stuff that shows up like `com.foo.Interface9`.

I suspect these are also what Alexander is referring to as "ad-hoc changes".

> You can look at converting Sensor values from int -> double as an example of this. Not sure how we could've accomplished that in a PDI client.

We've actually gone through these exact changes.  It depends on the complexity but there are two approaches we've done:

1. Just change the type and if the users have done enough `decltype`-like declarations it just works.  This typically works for int to size_t style changes.

2. A process like this:
    a. Temporarily add a new property Foo2 with the new type, have the daemon implement both.
    b. Convert the clients to the new Foo2.
    c. Have the daemon make Foo the new type also.
    d. Move all clients back to Foo2.
    
Not too long ago I did (2) for phosphor-logging to change the AdditionalData property from an array to a dict.

Something like (2) really isn't much different from what we'd have to do with hand-spun interfaces except that we also get compiler assistance when using the PDI bindings rather than just searching for strings and hoping for correctness.

Maintainers will have to make their own decision if they want to use it,
but we will require some amount of help to enable this possibility.

#### hesitation of rewrites of working code

Some folks may just not want to go through the effort of migrating their code to use PDI, or may not see the value in reviewing those changes to code that's already working and tested.

#### minimizing scope of design to secure approvals

I need votes on this design from a number of maintainers so i am carefully choosing the scope to provide a very specific solution with a minimum amount of work. 

This is why i went (based on feedback) from the initial approach of multiple object paths to a design where we only change what's the most problematic thing (the interfaces with index suffix).

#### amount of changes will be large for even this simple change

The changes that will need reviewing in e.g. `dbus-sensors` are to change for example the thresholds parsing to be done as per the design.

The thresholds alone are already a *large* amount of code on clients side and bmcweb side.

It may be quite some time before we can flip the switch in EM to stop exposing index-suffixed interfaces.

#### respecting the time available for community reviews

With this design we are already asking a lot by requesting review for the required changes.

Reviewing refactors of clients to use PDI is putting too much on maintainers who are already struggling to find time for other reviews, so we can leave that out of this design.
Added the reasoning for limiting the scope of the changes to be done.
